verses.sanskrit: अनित्यमेतद्देहमधिष्ठाय भूतग्रामम् अहं को 'स्मीति वेत्ति यः स ब्रह्म विदित्वा ||
verses.transliteration: anityametaddehamadhiṣṭhāya bhūtagrāmam ahaṃ ko'smīti vetti yaḥ sa brahma viditvā ||
verses.translation: Having inhabited this impermanent body composed of the aggregate of elements — who am I? One who truly knows this has known Brahman.
verses.hindi: इस अनित्य देह में, पंचभूतों के समूह में प्रविष्ट होकर — "मैं कौन हूँ?" जो यह जानता है, उसने ब्रह्म को जान लिया।
verses.commentary: Brihadratha's spiritual crisis — standing in the forest having renounced everything — is the authentic starting point of the Maitri. He does not begin with a doctrine; he begins with the raw question: in this body that will decay, among these elements that are impermanent — who am I? This is the question the Maitri will spend 230 verses answering. The honesty of the question is itself the beginning of the answer.
verses.wordMeaning: Brihadratha's spiritual crisis — standing in the forest having renounced everything — is the authentic starting point of the Maitri. He does not begin with a doctrine; he begins with the raw question: in this body that will decay, among these elements that are impermanent — who am I? This is the question the Maitri will spend 230 verses answering. The honesty of the question is itself the beginning of the answer.

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो आत्मसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogo ātmasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on the Self.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग आत्मा पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of Self-realization. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of the Self.
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of Self-realization. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of the Self.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं आत्मा एव सर्वं आत्मा मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ ātmā eva sarvaṃ ātmā mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is the Self alone, all is the Self in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब आत्मा ही है, सब आत्मा मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with the Self as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is the Self; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with the Self as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is the Self; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो आत्मनि लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo ātmani līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into the Self. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव आत्मा में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into the Self. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into the Self. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणायामः प्रत्याहारो ध्यानं धारणा तर्कः समाधिः षडङ्ग इत्युच्यते योगः ||
verses.transliteration: prāṇāyāmaḥ pratyāhāro dhyānaṃ dhāraṇā tarkaḥ samādhiḥ ṣaḍaṅga ityucyate yogaḥ ||
verses.translation: Pranayama, pratyahara, dhyana, dharana, tarka, samadhi — this sixfold practice is called yoga.
verses.hindi: प्राणायाम, प्रत्याहार, ध्यान, धारणा, तर्क और समाधि — इस षडङ्ग को योग कहते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Maitri Upanishad gives one of the earliest systematic descriptions of yoga — centuries before Patanjali's Yoga Sutras. The sequence is precise: first regulate the breath (pranayama), then withdraw the senses from their objects (pratyahara), then sustain focused attention on one object (dhyana), then hold that attention steadily (dharana), then apply discriminative reasoning (tarka), then allow the dissolution of the observer into the observed (samadhi). Each step prepares the conditions for the next.
verses.wordMeaning: The Maitri Upanishad gives one of the earliest systematic descriptions of yoga — centuries before Patanjali's Yoga Sutras. The sequence is precise: first regulate the breath (pranayama), then withdraw the senses from their objects (pratyahara), then sustain focused attention on one object (dhyana), then hold that attention steadily (dharana), then apply discriminative reasoning (tarka), then allow the dissolution of the observer into the observed (samadhi). Each step prepares the conditions for the next.

verses.sanskrit: यथा अग्निर्ज्वलनं निःश्वस्य न विद्यते | यथा सूर्यो रश्मीन् निगृह्य आस्ते | तथैव योगी विहाय सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: yathā agnirvālanaṃ niḥśvasya na vidyate | yathā sūryo raśmīn nigṛhya āste | tathāiva yogī vihāya sarvam ||
verses.translation: As fire without fuel is not found, as the sun withdraws its rays and simply is — so the yogi, having relinquished everything, simply is.
verses.hindi: जैसे अग्नि ईंधन के बिना नहीं रहती, जैसे सूर्य अपनी किरणें समेट लेता है — उसी प्रकार योगी, सब कुछ त्यागकर, बस रहता है।
verses.commentary: The most beautiful image of samadhi in the Maitri: the yogi is not extinguished like a fire without fuel — rather, he is like the sun that withdraws its rays but continues to shine. The rays are withdrawn into the source; the activity ceases but the being remains. Samadhi is not annihilation but the return of energy to its source — a state of being without doing, presence without agenda.
verses.wordMeaning: The most beautiful image of samadhi in the Maitri: the yogi is not extinguished like a fire without fuel — rather, he is like the sun that withdraws its rays but continues to shine. verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं आत्मा नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ ātmā nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual Self — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत आत्मा — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of the Self: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of the Self: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो आत्मानं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo ātmānaṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows the Self in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो आत्मा को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
